messages:
Noah: Hi team, on my first week trying the repo's CI. GitHub Actions runs but the publish step fails with 403 when trying to push to our ECR mirror. Error: "no basic auth credentials". Not sure which secret or permission I need.

liz: welcome Noah! For GH Actions you need the org secret for AWS creds (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) or use OIDC with role switching. If this is a fork GH won't forward org secrets.

Noah: it's not a fork, it's the org repo. I can see ECR_REGISTRY set in repo secrets but no AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. I thought the Actions runner role might handle it.

infra-bot: Tip: run a quick debug step in your workflow: `- run: aws sts get-caller-identity` to see which principal the runner is using. If that returns an IAM role from our infra account then OIDC is working.

Noah: ran it, got `arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/github-actions-runner`. So runner role exists. But the push still 403.

liz: 403 often means the role lacks ECR push permissions or the registry account doesn't match. Confirm the role trust policy and attached policy include `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken` and the upload actions. Also check the registry host in `docker login` matches `444455556666`.

Noah: the registry was pointing to 555566667777.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com, which is different. I bet someone copied an example.

liz: yep that's it. Either update ECR_REGISTRY to the right account or add cross-account permissions. For onboarding we usually update the secret to the correct registry and grant the runner role a scoped policy.

Noah: updated secret to 444455556666 and re-ran.

ci-bot: Workflow run #9 failed at step "login-and-push" with 403

Noah: still 403, hmm. I added the AWS secrets temporarily to the repo secrets (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) and re-ran and it worked. So GH OIDC runner role is missing ecr permissions.

liz: I'll add a short onboarding note: for GH Actions OIDC you need the role to include this managed policy snippet for ECR push (onboarding minimal): `{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["ecr:GetAuthorizationToken","ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability","ecr:InitiateLayerUpload","ecr:UploadLayerPart","ecr:CompleteLayerUpload","ecr:PutImage"],"Resource":"*"}]}`. For prod scope it down to specific registry ARNs.

Noah: adding that to my onboarding doc now. Thanks! Learned three things: confirm registry account, check whether GH forwards org secrets, and verify runner role policies or fallback to repo secrets for onboarding. :+1:

liz: if you want I can open a PR to add the check to our CI preflight step to validate registry/account before trying to push.

Noah: please do, that would have saved me an hour. Thanks everyone!
